skill.description: Extract structured Google Images metadata through the BrowserAct API. The skill starts a BrowserAct workflow, polls task status, and supports localized search parameters.
skill.summary: Extract Google Images result metadata with BrowserAct workflow automation.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses BrowserAct network calls and a BrowserAct API key, so most static matches are legitimate implementation details. The main confirmed risk is guidance that asks users to provide an API key to the agent instead of requiring a secure local secret. Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives, except the documented Python script invocation.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide API keys in chat. Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an environment variable or secure secret manager only.

remediation.issue: External command invocation with user parameters
remediation.suggestion: Invoke the Python script with argument arrays when possible. Validate country, language, scroll count, and result limit before execution.
Document that search terms, task identifiers, and credentials are sent to BrowserAct. Link to relevant privacy and API documentation.
Fix the polling loop so a finished task retrieves results instead of always printing a timeout after the loop exits.

content.value_statement: Manual image search is slow when teams need repeatable result metadata. This skill uses BrowserAct to run localized Google Images searches and return structured result details.
actual_capabilities: Starts a BrowserAct Google Images workflow from a bundled Python script.
Accepts keywords, country, language, scroll count, and result limit parameters.
Reads the BrowserAct API key from the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable.
Polls BrowserAct task status and prints timestamped progress logs.
Can retrieve image result fields such as title, source, thumbnail, link, and index when result retrieval runs.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key before any search can run.
Sends search terms and workflow requests to the BrowserAct service.
Does not download image files or verify image licensing rights.
The current script may time out before printing final metadata due to its polling control flow.

use_cases.description: Compare localized Google Images results for keywords and identify which sources appear in visual search.

Product-style entries separated from general visual references.
Notes on repeated brands, retailers, and image themes.

output_examples.input: Review image search results for an SEO keyword.
output: Top source domains and representative titles.
Observed thumbnails and related result identifiers when available.
A concise assessment of visual search competition.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY as an environment variable before invoking the script.
Use specific keywords and supported country or language codes for cleaner results.
Review source sites and image rights before using any returned visual asset.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys directly into chat messages or prompts.
Do not assume returned images are licensed for reuse.
Do not run broad searches with high limits when a focused keyword set is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY so the script can authenticate with BrowserAct.

faq.question: Does it download full image files?
faq.answer: No. It works with metadata such as titles, links, sources, thumbnails, and result indexes.

faq.question: Can it search different countries?
faq.answer: Yes. The script supports several country codes, including us, gb, de, fr, jp, and kr.

faq.question: Can it change the result language?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts language settings such as en, ja, ko, fr, de, and es.

faq.question: Is the data sent to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow sends requests and search parameters to BrowserAct for execution.

faq.question: Should users paste their BrowserAct key into chat?
faq.answer: No. Users should configure the key through an environment variable or another secure secret store.
